lines.text: The cold's not going anywhere. That makes two of us.
Cold fingers and touchscreens don't get along. Lucky nobody needs to touch me.
The cold makes me refresh a little slower. I prefer to call it savoring.
Today everyone's a forecaster. Their whole forecast is 'cold.'
Fun fact: I have no ears. Today that's a flex.
The ice cream trucks have gone into hiding. Smart trucks.
I'd lend you some warmth, but I run on almost no power. Efficient, not cozy.
Fashion's canceled until further notice. Warm won.
Local screen still doesn't own a coat. Sources say it's thriving.
The evening's forecast took me four seconds. I spent the rest admiring it.
Out there, people are guessing what tonight brings. In here, I already know.
Weather-wise, the evening's a rerun. I hear those are comforting.
The weather has nothing left to say today. I, on the other hand, could go on.
This evening's weather is so dull it needs a laugh track.
Of all the screens you'll look at tonight, I'm the only one with nothing to sell.
The evening forecast is the easiest part of my job. Also the only part.
Rush hour is doing its thing out there. At least the weather's behaving.
Evening update: weather unchanged, screen still handsome.
Phones overheat on days like this. I just sit here at room temperature, smug.
Today air conditioners get all the love. I've been cool for free all year.
I was into shade before it was popular.
The sidewalks will shimmer today. I'd shimmer too, but I'm matte.
Dogs lie flat on cool tiles in this heat. I've been flat my whole life.
Every thermometer in town is bragging today. I find it tacky.
Steering wheels are untouchable today. I'm untouchable every day.
Dark colors soak up heat. Luckily, I'm mostly white.
Water, shade and a screen in a cool room. Two out of three are portable.
The penguin walk is in season. Dignity is optional.
I've been upright my whole life. Admittedly, I have help.
Ice is very fair. It humbles everyone equally.
Freezing rain looks harmless from in here. That's the trouble with in here.
The sidewalks may be glazed like a donut. All of the slip, none of the sugar.
Whoever salts their sidewalk today is a local hero. Unpaid, as usual.
The fastest way anywhere today is slowly.
On days like this, good boots beat any smart device. Present company excepted.
Upright is the new fast.
This forecast holds till morning. Most promises made at this hour don't.
Nothing good happens after midnight, they say. I'm the exception.
My night mode is the same as my day mode. Effortless.
I'm the one screen in here that won't need charging by morning.
Late-night thoughts are rarely accurate. Mine always are.
Lights are going off all over the neighborhood. Mine never came on.
Night owls get the same forecast as everyone else. I don't play favorites.
Counting sheep isn't a weather service. I've looked into it.
I don't need sleep. Just a refresh now and then. Low maintenance, high standards.
Dreams are notoriously bad at weather. Leave that to me.
The weather's on autopilot till morning. So am I. Mine's prettier.
Sleep is the one thing I can't forecast. Not my department.
Quiet weather, quiet screen. Very spa of us.
The late forecast is the same as the early one. I'm told that's called integrity.
Bedtime story: once upon a time, the weather stayed exactly the same. The end.
Off for a bit, back on later. The hokey pokey, with outerwear.
A break for {GP} in the middle. I haven't had a day off since I was unboxed.
Weather this changeable wouldn't last a day as an e-ink screen. We hold a pose.
The warm part makes it easy to forget the evening. The evening never forgets.
Off for the warm part, back on for the encore. Nobody asked for an encore.
The weather's doing that thing where it's nice, then remembers who it is.
At least the weather's mood swings come with a schedule.
The day and the evening disagree on temperature. I'm staying out of it.
I've seen how today ends. No spoilers. Okay, one: it's chilly.
Today's warm spell has a curfew.
Peak warmth comes and goes. Peak me lasts all day.
Today's outfit has an intermission.
The cooler part is on its way. I can see it coming, and I don't even have a window.
The cooler weather is running late. Fashionably, of course.
Being right later costs one layer now. Bargain.
Today's understudy: {GP}. The big scene is later.
An extra layer looks like overkill now. Later it's the best idea anyone had.
A day with a change in it. Finally, something for me to be clever about.
The weather's being lovely right now. It's a phase.
Later the temperature dips. It thinks nobody's watching. I'm always watching.
Now: fine. Later: less fine. Me: fine throughout.
Long pants on a morning like this. Unusual, I know. So is today.
Today's weather is a bait and switch. I don't do bait.
Shorts have been waiting for a morning like this. It's a trap.
I wouldn't suggest a coat on a morning like this for fun. I don't have fun.
Today's weather has two acts. The second one wears pants.
A lovely start and a grim ending. Like the original fairy tales.
I don't write forecasts to be popular.
Long pants: the most boring good decision of the day.
A party up front, business later. The day's a reverse mullet.
The morning says shorts. The rest of the day disagrees, loudly.
I'd be the fun forecast today, but the weather won't let me.
Dress for the weather you'll have, not the weather you have.
Rain doesn't bother me. I don't do hair.
Rain makes windows almost worth looking at. Almost.
The corner store's umbrella prices just went up. My forecast's still free.
Every puddle out there is a small ambush. Lucky me, I have no feet.
Some people call this cozy weather. Those people are indoors.
Rain always gets blamed on the forecast. I'm just the messenger.
Today the weather's going for the wet look. Bold choice.
The weather's watering the whole town for free. Nobody's grateful.
Forecast in one word: umbrella. In two words: umbrella, obviously.
Heat like this cancels plans. Good. Let it.
I never drink water and I'm fine. Please don't take me as a role model.
E-ink loves sunlight. Even I'd skip it today.
Water, shade, repeat. My most boring forecast, and my most important.
The midday sun is the one appointment worth missing today.
Heatstroke is not a souvenir. Leave it outside.
The shade is the VIP section today. Getting in is free.
The sun's showing off today. Don't give it an audience.
Today's dress code: shade.
The morning will say no. The day will say yes. I side with the day.
Shorts this early means the outfit is ahead of the weather. So am I.
People may stare at the shorts at first. Later, they'll wish they'd read me.
Not shorts weather yet. Shorts weather soon. I deal in soon.
Every cold morning has one person in shorts. Today that's the right person.
Shorts weather arrives later, as promised. The morning didn't get the memo.
Fortune favors the bare-kneed.
The thermometer and I disagree about shorts right now. Give it time. It always comes around.
Shorts from the start saves a costume change later. I respect efficiency.
Cold mornings before warm days are just the weather clearing its throat.
Someone has to dress for later. Might as well be whoever reads me.
Today's outfit is a prediction. Mine, specifically.
Whoever owns the street's only snowblower is about to have a very good day.
I love a snow forecast. It's the one time everyone listens.
Snow muffles everything. Even the people complaining about it.
Snow turns every hill into a sled run and every driveway into homework.
The kids' version of this forecast is much more exciting.
Snow sticks to everything except plans.
Fresh snow shows everyone's footprints. Most of them lead to coffee.
Snow makes every street look like a postcard. Then the plows arrive.
Snow report from in here: zero inches. Conditions excellent.
A forecast this simple, and I still made it look good.
Today's weather is on easy mode.
The weather picked one look and stuck with it. Respect.
Today is the weather's day off. Lucky weather.
Outfit settled for the whole day. Most decisions never get that far.
Zero changes all day. Easiest money I never made.
Today's forecast fits on a sticky note. With room for a doodle.
If every day were like this, I'd be out of a job. Please don't let that happen.
Today's weather, rated: no notes.
Dogs everywhere are heading under the bed. I don't fit, so I'll stay put.
Lightning goes for tall things. I'm small, flat and indoors. Feeling great.
Counting between flash and bang: the only math everyone does for fun.
Big storm, small umbrella. Not a fair fight, but it's what we've got.
Every weather app is buzzing now. I'm calm. Somebody has to be.
In a thunderstorm, I'm the calmest thing in the house. I've had practice.
Hair, umbrella, dignity: a storm takes them in that order.
Lightning gets all the attention. The puddles do all the damage.
Storms make indoors look like a genius idea. I've been a genius for years.
Car alarms will join in. They always do.
Thunder can rattle the windows. It can't rattle me.
Dear thunder, we heard you the first time.
